prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Summary of key proposals (non-exhaustive)

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self-employed NI during the next Parliament.
- Maintain rates of income tax and VAT; introduce a “Triple Lock Plus” so the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation, or 2.5%.
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; move Child Benefit to a household test starting taper at £120,000.
- Business: retain full expensing (explore extension to leasing), no rise in corporation tax, 10-point SME plan (business rates relief focus, prompt payments, Open Finance, regional mutual banks, keep key investment incentives).
- Regulation/Whitehall: reduce civil service to pre-pandemic size; halve spend on consultants; relocate roles out of London; expand digital/AI capability; Minimum Service Levels on strikes.

Infrastructure, innovation and trade
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 Phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, bus), including Northern Powerhouse Rail (Manchester–Liverpool) and Midlands Rail Hub; electrify North Wales Main Line.
- Nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; legal framework for automated vehicles; aviation SAF support; maritime connectivity review.
- R&D to £22bn/year; invest in compute for AI; advanced manufacturing plan; maintain R&D tax reliefs; support financial services competitiveness.
- Trade: implement CPTPP; pursue FTAs with India and GCC; deepen EU TCA without ceding sovereignty; maintain standards in NHS and food.

Education, skills and youth
- Ban mobile phones in school day; give parents access to curriculum materials; protect per-pupil funding in real terms.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19 (broader study, English and maths to 18).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor-outcome degree courses.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or part-time civic service).

Welfare and work
- Tighten work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes via specialist teams; reform PIP with greater focus on needs and treatment access; stronger sanctions for long-term non-compliance; fraud bill to bolster DWP powers.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First, modernise GP premises, add 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade: NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, data platforms; reduce managers by 5,500.
- Dental recovery plan (more NHS appointments, contract reform, rural “golden hellos”, vans); require new dentists to serve in NHS for a period or repay training.
- Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions (maternity safety, pelvic health, hubs); implement Cass Review; single-sex accommodation rights; expand youth/adult mental health access.

Borders, security and defence
- Legal annual cap on work/family migration that falls each year; raise salary thresholds; health checks and higher charges; restrict dependants; increase visa fees; expand returns deals.
- Monthly removals to Rwanda; seek international asylum reform; intensify organised immigration crime action.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; Defence Innovation Agency with 5% of budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; sustained support to Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and benefits.

Policing, justice, and civic order
- 8,000 additional neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; facial recognition and anti-knife powers; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences for serious offenders; four new prisons; more foreign offender removals; expand fraud measures.
- New protest controls (e.g., face coverings bans, cumulative impact); protect schools from targeted protests; counter-extremism measures.

Energy, climate and environment
- Annual North Sea oil/gas licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; two CCS clusters now and more later; expedite small modular reactors and approve Wylfa; expand interconnectors.
- Keep energy price cap; review standing charges; energy-efficiency vouchers and £6bn for home upgrades; onshore wind with local consent; solar away from best farmland; no fracking.
- Environment: deliver biodiversity targets, expand Blue Belt, moratorium on deep-sea mining, strengthen water regulation and penalties, river restoration fund, tree planting and urban greening, tougher fly-tipping penalties, deposit return scheme, limit new incinerators.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes in England; lift nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; fast-track brownfield; densify inner London; protect Green Belt.
- Permanent SDLT relief for first-time buyers up to £425k; new Help to Buy; CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants; complete leasehold reform; renters’ reform with Section 21 abolition alongside court changes.
- £20m endowments for 105 towns; extend Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports and zones; Backing Drivers Bill (ban road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, local referendums for 20mph/LTNs); extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.

Food, rural and coastal
- Increase UK-wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament with inflation protection; legal food security target; 50% public food spend local/higher-standard; fast-track farm infrastructure; seasonal worker scheme with taper; £100m Seafood Fund successor; expand inshore opportunities; major flood defence investment.

Union and devolution
- Protect internal market and unfettered trade; extend UK-wide funds and investment zones; specific transport, energy, and industry projects across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland; support for Windsor Framework implementation and legacy bodies.

TEXT_G:
Summary of key proposals (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and taxes: Responsible fiscal rules with OBR oversight; repair trade with Europe; industrial strategy focused on green, digital and biosciences; expand British Business Bank; tackle tax avoidance; reverse bank tax cuts; one‑off windfall tax on oil and gas; raise Digital Services Tax; fairer capital gains; 4% levy on FTSE‑100 buybacks; priority future income tax cut via higher personal allowance; national financial inclusion strategy.

- Business and work: Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; strengthen late‑payment rules; local banking for SMEs; employee ownership rights; public‑interest takeover test widened; skills and training levy replacing apprenticeship levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim to £10,000); National Colleges; gig‑economy “dependent contractor” status and rights; stronger sick pay from day one; Worker Protection Authority; living wage review; AI regulatory framework; Parliament to sign off trade deals.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% renewable electricity by 2030; 10‑year home energy upgrade with free insulation/heat pumps for low‑income homes; zero‑carbon new buildings; social energy tariff; decouple power prices from gas; end fossil fuel subsidies with just transition; lift barriers to wind/solar; no fracking or new coal; grid expansion, storage and interconnectors; boost community energy; UK ETS–EU ETS linkage; carbon border adjustment; industry decarbonisation support.

- Health: Right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours urgent), 8,000 more GPs, expanded pharmacy roles and 24/7 booking; urgent access to NHS dentistry and prevention measures; mental health hubs for young people and regular check‑ups; a mental health professional in every school; cancer treatment within 62 days, more cancer nurses and equipment; workforce retention plan and independent pay review; ambulance handover fixes; hospital estate renewal; interoperable digital records; evidence‑led drug policy including a regulated cannabis market; fair hospice funding.

- Social care and carers: Free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers and a higher Carer’s Minimum Wage; cross‑party funding settlement; paid carer’s leave and regular respite; personal budgets, portability of care packages, National Care Agency; support for kinship care; healthy ageing programmes.

- Education and skills: School/college funding rises above inflation; building repairs; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; early‑years boost and higher Early Years Pupil Premium; reinstate university maintenance grants; teacher pay/CPD strategy; curriculum and assessment reform; SEND funding overhaul; arts protected; extracurricular expansion; Young People’s Premium (16–18); Erasmus+ return; university duty of care and mental health charter.

- Families: Extend free school meals to children in poverty; Minister for Children; day‑one parental leave/pay (incl. self‑employed); double statutory maternity/shared parental pay; higher, use‑it‑or‑lose‑it leave for partners; childcare funding review and workforce plan.

- Safety net and pensions: Scrap two‑child limit and benefit cap; target ending deep poverty; UC first payment in five days; end sanctions regime; scrap bedroom tax; protect the pension triple lock; fair treatment for 1950s‑born women; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance; disability benefit and assessment reforms.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and proper investigation of burglaries; Online Crime Agency; invest to cut court backlogs; scrap Police and Crime Commissioners; tackle disproportionate stop and search; domestic abuse specialists; mental‑health handover target; halve offence‑to‑sentence times; youth diversion duty; anti‑fraud reimbursement; modern slavery protections; prison rehab and resettlement.

- Natural environment: Tougher water regulation, public‑benefit model and bonus bans until discharges end; binding targets to “double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and new Air Quality Agency; stronger watchdogs; sewage tax, real‑time discharge data and stricter targets; expand accessible green space and National Nature Parks; Environmental Rights Act; stronger biodiversity net‑gain and land/sea use framework; deposit return scheme; eliminate non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; peat and marine protection.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund Environmental Land Management (+£1bn/yr); maintain high standards in trade; veterinary and plant‑health agreements with Europe; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; rural infrastructure; reduce pesticides/fertilisers; research fund incl. alternative proteins; robust labelling; comprehensive animal welfare law.

- Housing: Build 380,000 homes/year, incl. 150,000 social; ten new garden cities; zero‑carbon new homes; ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register; allow ending Right to Buy locally; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; remove unsafe cladding at no cost to leaseholders; Rent‑to‑Own for social housing; planning reforms, brownfield incentives, “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it”; end rough sleeping and repeal the Vagrancy Act.

- Local government and communities: Multi‑year council funding; powers over second homes/short‑lets (new planning class, up to 500% council‑tax premium, surcharge on overseas buyers); gigabit broadband nationwide; decentralisation; protect community assets; rural transport powers; Rural Fuel Duty Relief.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout, grid upgrades, card payments and 5% VAT on public charging; reinstate plug‑in grant; 2030 zero‑emission sales rule for cars/vans; freeze rail fares and simplify tickets; new Railway Agency; enforce operator standards; major rail electrification and Northern Powerhouse Rail; bus franchising powers and £2 fare cap; active travel networks; more road‑maintenance funding; reform aviation taxes, curb private jets, ban short domestic flights where rail <2.5h.

- Culture, media and sport: Protect public service broadcasters; creative skills and finance access; simple EU/UK touring arrangements; Creative Europe participation; anti‑SLAPP law; independent press regulation; ticket resale clampdown; problem‑gambling levy, affordability checks; football regulator with fan voice.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy to relevant departments; scrap recent unlawful‑migration measures and Rwanda plan; uphold Refugee Convention; safe and legal routes; three‑month asylum decision standard; right to work after three months; flexible work‑visa criteria; exemptions for health/care; reverse family visa threshold rises; protect EU citizens with Settled Status and physical proof; Windrush redress independent; repeal Right to Rent; expand legal aid.

- Rights and equality: Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; Race Equality Strategy; make misogyny a hate crime; day‑one flexible working and work‑from‑home right for disabled people; ban conversion practices; repeal recent anti‑protest measures; Digital Bill of Rights and biometric regulation; expand VAWG services; humanist marriages; limited rights for cohabitees; protect reproductive rights; modernise gender recognition incl. non‑binary; diversity reporting; disability employment support and BSL access; free vote on assisted dying.

- Political reform: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; scrap voter ID; legislate Ministerial Code; reform the Lords; cap donations; citizens’ assemblies; transparency on lobbying and digital communications; devolution within a federal framework; protect the Electoral Commission.

- Defence and security: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; stronger arms‑export controls; parliamentary vote before military action; procurement reform; improve housing, pay, and support for forces and veterans; strengthen intelligence oversight; deepen European defence cooperation and Five Eyes ties.

- International: Support rules‑based order; rebuild European relations via phased roadmap (incl. veterinary accords, agency participation, deeper trade and Single Market aim); stand with Ukraine and seize frozen Russian assets to fund support; restore ODA to 0.7% with an independent department; immediate bilateral ceasefire in Israel‑Gaza and two‑state solution with recognition of Palestine; targeted human‑rights sanctions and import bans from abuse regions; support Hong Kongers, Taiwan and Uyghurs; fund BBC World Service; prioritise education, climate and nutrition in aid.
